requirements.text: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

claude.basis: On net5+ consumers the attribute is emitted on every generated type (AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage passes at head and fails on base). But every emission is wrapped in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', which is evaluated in the consumer's compilation, so consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no attribute. The stated reason ('not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework') is wrong: System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is in the netstandard 2.0 reference assembly (I checked netstandard.library 2.0.3's netstandard.xml) and has been in .NET Framework since 4.0, with AttributeTargets.Class allowed. So for targets MessagePack supports, the requirement is not met, and a test pins the omission.

findings.title: Coverage attribute is suppressed for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers based on a false premise
findings.claim: The templates guard the attribute with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK'. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, so the guard only removes the feature for Unity/.NET Framework/netstandard library consumers. The test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable pins this behaviour, and the README claims 'All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated', which is false for those targets.

evidence.quote: All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`
evidence.note: quote matches README.md:1639 at head a0aa5ab2

findings.suggested_fix: Drop the #if guard and emit [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] unconditionally; replace the guard test with one that compiles generated code against a netstandard2.0 / net472 reference set.
